From 1 to 14 September you were rostered for 20 hours and were paid $440, which is $22 an hour. At the national minimum casual rate of $33.05 an hour, those 20 hours may have been worth about $661, a difference of about $221. This does not necessarily mean your employer did anything wrong: a different award may apply, there may be deductions you agreed to, or the hours you actually worked may differ from the roster.

Next steps:
• Check your rate with the Fair Work Pay Calculator
• Keep your rosters, timesheets and payslips
• A union or community legal centre can help for free
• Asking about your pay will not get your visa cancelled by your employer
